name: Santos
description: Identify the Santos by its square case with a rounded, screw-set bezel showing eight exposed screws and an integrated bracelet — one of the first purpose-built pilot's wristwatches. It may come in variants like: steel, two-tone gold-and-steel, and skeleton dials.

name: Tank
description: Identify the Tank by its rectangular case with strong vertical 'brancards' (the bars flanking the dial that echo a tank's tracks), Roman numerals, a railway minute track, blued sword hands, and a sapphire cabochon crown. It may come in variants like: Tank Louis, Tank Must, Tank Française, and Tank Américaine.

name: Panthère
description: Identify the Panthère as a compact, jewellery-like square watch — like a shrunken Santos but without the exposed bezel screws. Look for the small square case with rounded corners, Roman numerals over a fine inner rail track, blued sword hands, a sapphire cabochon crown, and a supple polished multi-link integrated bracelet (some versions add a diamond-set bezel).

name: Ballon Bleu
description: Identify the Ballon Bleu by its rounded case with a blue sapphire cabochon crown tucked into a protective bulge that arcs over the dial, Roman numerals, and a railway track. It may come in variants like: silver dial, and steel or two-tone cases across several sizes.

name: Pasha
description: Identify the Pasha by its round case with bold Arabic numerals at 12, 3, 6 and 9 set over an inner square 'rail' track, blued hands, and a date window near 4 o'clock. Its signature is the screw-down crown cover — a round cap (often chained) with a cabochon that protects the crown.

name: Drive
description: Identify the Drive by its cushion-shaped (coussin) case — a rounded square with gently curved flanks. This reference carries a silvered guilloché dial with Roman numerals, a large date at 12, a retrograde second-time-zone indicator, a small-seconds sub-dial, a day/night aperture, and blued hands.

name: Ronde
description: Identify the Ronde as the plainest round Cartier: a thin polished bezel, a silvered dial with Roman numerals over a railway minute track, blued sword hands, a date window at 3, and 'AUTOMATIC' script above six. Clean and time-focused, without the arcing crown guard of the Ballon Bleu.

name: Tortue
description: Identify the Tortue by its tortoise-shell-shaped case — an elongated cushion with gently curved flanks that taper toward the lugs. Look for a guilloché dial with Roman numerals, slim hands, and a sapphire cabochon crown. Elegant and typically time-only.

name: Baignoire
description: Identify the Baignoire by its elongated oval 'bathtub' case — much longer than it is wide, with fully rounded ends. Look for a silvered dial with elongated Roman numerals curving to follow the oval, blued hands, and a cabochon crown. A distinctive, decorative dress shape.

name: Clé
description: Identify the Clé by its round polished case with distinctive curved, notched lugs and a blue sapphire cabochon set into the crown at 3 o'clock — the crown shaped like a winding key gives the model its name. Look for a silvered flinqué guilloché dial, blue Roman numerals over a fine minute track, blued sword hands, and a date window at 6.
